info.title: SSL Web Services (SWS) API
info.description:
SSL.com SSL Web Services (SWS) API is a PKI service that allows life-cycle management of X.509 digital certificates. Please refer to this guide for more details.

To get pregenerated API cURL commands for an individual order, append /developer to the end of that certificate order page (e.g. https://www.ssl.com/certificate_orders/co-1234xyz/developer).

Security: Most requests require that your account_key and secret_key be sent. You can set these values using the Authorize 🔒 link below. These values are available from the api credentials link on the Dashboard of your SSL.com Sandbox account. (See this guide for information on setting up your free Sandbox account.)

For API documentation about SSL.com's CSC and eSigner.com cloud and remote signing interfaces, please refer to:

  • Remote Document Signing with eSigner CSC API
  • Remote EV Code Signing with eSigner
  • Integration Guide to Testing Remote Signing with eSigner CSC API
  • Postman API Profiles

get.summary: Get a list of purchased certificates.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of records per page (default is 10 if unspecified).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number. Example: if per_page is set to 10, and page is 5, then records 51-60 will be returned.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Beginning of date range when the certificate orders were created. Example: 01-31-2012

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Ending of date range when the certificate orders were created. If not specified then defaults to now. Example: 04-30-2015

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter the result set. Currently vouchers is supported and only returns unused available certificate order credits. If this parameter is not specified all certificate orders are returned. Example: vouchers

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Advanced search by criteria such as product, expiration, certificate fields, etc.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Return only the requested fields

post.description: Create an SSL.com certificate order or voucher code. Upon a successful API call, the price (if any) of the certificate will be deducted from the account associated with the account_key specified in the call. Voucher codes are used to purchase a certificate without having to submit a CSR right away. This is useful for host providers, enterprise environments, or any situation where buying the certificate and installing it do not necessarily happen at the same time. A voucher code can be created by specifying the product type and duration but not providing a CSR.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
**String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.** 

**Example: `co-abcd1234`**

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description:
**Specifies the type/format of the certificates that are being returned, if applicable. Default: `individually`**
  + zip
  + netscape
  + pkcs7
  + individually

parameters.name: response_encoding
parameters.description:
**Specifies the encoding of the certificates that are being returned, if applicable. Default: `base64`**
  + base64
  + binary

put.summary: Process, rekey, or update validation of an SSL Certificate order.
put.description:
Use this call to process a voucher, rekey an existing certificate order, or change the validation method(s).

To process a voucher, simply provide the voucher code ref along with the csr and other relevant information for the certificate order. This also applies to a certificate that has already been processed but needs to be rekeyed.

To change the validation methods, simply provide the voucher or certificate reference number ref and the domains parameter. The other "required" parameters are not required if doing the update validation call.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
**String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.** 

**Example: `co-abcd1234`**

delete.description: Use this call to revoke an issued certificate based on it's serial number, or all issued certificates under a specific order using its certificate reference or voucher number.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
**String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.** 

**Example: `co-abcd1234`**

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description:
**The reason for this revocation. If there is a different reason for each certificate, then each certificate should be individually revoked through its own API call.**
  

**Example: `mistake`**

parameters.name: serials
parameters.description:
**The serial numbers of one or more issued certificates under this order. If no serial numbers are specified, then all issued certificates will be revoked for the certificate order identified by the ref parameter.**
  


**Example:  `["0c:00:99:b7:d7:89:c9:f6:66:26:31:7e:bc:ea:7c:1c"]`**

get.summary: Retrieve acceptable domain validation methods for a certificate.
get.description: A single Validation object containing a list of acceptable methods to complete the verification of the order.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
**String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.** 

**Example: `co-abcd1234`**

post.summary: Retrieve acceptable email addresses for domain control validation.
post.description: A single Validation object containing a list of acceptable email addresses for domain control control validation of a certificate.

post.summary: Retrieve all validation methods based on hash of certificate signing request
post.description: A single Validation object containing values that will satisfy domain control validation using the hash of the certificate signing request.

get.summary: Retrieve pre-filled parameters needed to make a successful API call
get.description: A list of pre-filled parameters needed to make a successful API call

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description:
**String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.** 

**Example: `co-abcd1234`**

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
**This is the valid action that API intends to call. The returned parameters can then be used in that API action call. Valid actions are: `update_dcv`, `update`, `create_w_csr`, `create`, `show`, `index`, `dcv_emails`, `dcv_methods_wo_csr`, and `dcv_methods_w_csr`. Please note that some actions cannot be executed such as `update_dcv` if the CSR has not already been submitted.** 

**Example: `create`**

domains.description:
Domains to be included in the certificate. These values override those listed in the certificate signing request (CSR). If domains is not specified, the domains for the certificate order will be extracted from the CSR. If you want to use some or all of the domains encoded in the CSR along with some additional domains, then you must list all domains in this parameter. The first domain listed in the hash is by default listed in the CN field and the other domains will be listed in the SAN field. Multiple domains can only be listed for the following products: 100, 102, 107. Other product types will only use the first domain and ignore the other domains.

Example (when CSR is specified)
{"www.mysite.com": {"dcv": "admin@mysite.com"}, "mail.domain.io": {"dcv: "HTTP_CSR_HASH"}}
 Example (when csr is not specified)
["www.mysite.com","*.test.com","mail.yoursite.com"]

organization.description:
Sets the Organization (O) field of the certificate to this value. Ignored for DV certificates.
Overrides the (O) value in the CSR if csr is specified.
Example: SSL Corp

organization_unit.description:
Sets the Organization Unit (OU) (eg department name). Ignored for DV certificates.
Overrides the (OU) value in the CSR if csr is specified.

callback.description:
This is the callback SSL.com will make once the certificate is issued and ready for collection. The URL is "called" via the method (POST or GET).
  • url (required, string) The URL (must use https) that SSL.com will call to notify that the certificate is issued and ready.
  • <method (required, string) The HTTP method used in the URL callback. Valid values are:
    • get Can only be notified of the certificate issuance status via the status_hook parameter (see below)
    • post Can receive the certificate chain via the certificate_hook parameter (see below)

domains.description:
Domains to be included in the certificate. These values override those listed in the certificate signing request (CSR). If domains is not specified, the domains for the certificate order will be extracted from the CSR. If you want to use some or all of the domains encoded in the CSR along with some additional domains, then you must list all domains in this parameter. The first domain listed in the hash is by default listed in the CN field and the other domains will be listed in the SAN field. Multiple domains can only be listed for the following products: 100, 102, 107. Other product types will only use the first domain and ignore the other domains.

Example (when CSR is specified)
{"www.mysite.com": {"dcv": "admin@mysite.com"}, "mail.domain.io": {"dcv: "HTTP_CSR_HASH"}}
 Example (when csr is not specified)
["www.mysite.com","*.test.com","mail.yoursite.com"]

ref.name: ref
ref.description:
String ref is the certificate reference number (or voucher code) of the SSL.com certificate order. You specify this in the URL so there is no need to include it as a parameter in the JSON request.

Example: co-abcd1234

reason_required.name: reason
reason_required.description:
The reason for this revocation. If there is a different reason for each certificate, then each certificate should be individually revoked through its own API call.

Example:mistake

serials.name: serials
serials.description:
The serial numbers of one or more issued certificates under this order. If no serial numbers are specified, then all issued certificates will be revoked for the certificate order identified by the ref parameter.

Example:["0c:00:99:b7:d7:89:c9:f6:66:26:31:7e:bc:ea:7c:1c"]

action_required.name: action
action_required.description:

Valid actions are: update_dcv, update, create_w_csr, create, show, index, dcv_emails, dcv_methods_wo_csr, and dcv_methods_w_csr. Please note that some actions cannot be executed such as update_dcv if the CSR has not already been submitted.
